issues.body: `_validate_record` only rejects extra fields when `origin == ORIGIN_WRITE`; every other value, including a typo such as `"writ"`, falls through to `_tolerable_unknown_field` and is handled exactly like `ORIGIN_READ`. Requiring the argument but not validating its value therefore does not make a future call site declare its posture fail-closed, as the docstring and design record claim. A misspelled write-side constant would silently admit undeclared fields into the record-validation path. The self-test checks only that omitting the argument raises `TypeError`, so it cannot detect this failure mode.
issues.fix_hint: At the start of `_validate_record`, reject any `origin` not exactly in `{ORIGIN_READ, ORIGIN_WRITE}` with `ValueError` (or otherwise branch exhaustively). Add a non-vacuous test passing a literal invalid origin together with an undeclared field and assert the invalid origin is refused; retain the existing tests for the two valid postures.
issues.title: Unknown origin values silently select the permissive read posture

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The forward-compatible read behavior is carefully scoped and the added tests cover many important seams, but the new trust-boundary discriminator itself is not fail-closed. An invalid or misspelled origin silently receives read tolerance, so the implementation does not uphold its documented guarantee that call sites explicitly select one of the two postures.
